subject: Deducer: Syntax error in K-Sample Test, post-hoc t-test, correction Bonferroni

messages.author: e5eeb0c47fdbba84
messages.subject: Deducer: Syntax error in K-Sample Test, post-hoc t-test, correction Bonferroni
parts:
Dear all,

I found a reproducible syntax error when I run a K-Sample Test with
pairwise comparison (method t-Test, correction Bonferroni).

This is the output in the console

> k.sample.test(formula=d(depVar) ~ indepFactor,
+ data=demo,
+ test=oneway.test,var.equal=TRUE)
One-way analysis of
means
F (num df,denom df) p-value
depVar 14.70871 (2,27) 4.778948e-05
> pairwise.t.test(demo$depVar,demo$indepFactorpool.sd = TRUE, p.adjust.method = 'bonferroni')
Fehler: Unerwartete(s) '=' in "pairwise.t.test(demo$depVar,demo
$indepFactorpool.sd ="
>
The cause of the error is a missing comma before pool.sd. If you
correct it to:

pairwise.t.test(demo$depVar,demo$indepFactor, pool.sd = TRUE,
p.adjust.method = 'bonferroni')

The statistics is calculated.

Cheers

Karl-Heinz

messages.subject: Re: Deducer: Syntax error in K-Sample Test, post-hoc t-test, correction Bonferroni
parts:
Dear all,

I was just curious whether I could fix the problem myself, however, I
have to mention that I have not much experience in programming.

It looks to me as if the problem is located in the file: /org/rosuda/
deducer/menu/KSampleDialog.java line 438 in the latest svn source.
Beginning in line 435 the source currently looks like:

435 ... }else if(pairwiseMethod == "t-test (equal variance)"){
436 for(int i=0;i<variables.size();i++)
437 cmd += "pairwise.t.test(" +subn + "$" +
variables.get(i).toString() + "," +
438 subn + "$" + factor + "pool.sd = TRUE" +
439 ", p.adjust.method = '" + model.pairwiseCorrection +"')
\n";

My problem should be fixed with line 438 being changed to (note the
comma before pool.sd):

438 subn + "$" + factor + ", pool.sd = TRUE" +

I have no idea, how to upload this fix to the repository (I have never
worked with svn so far). It would be great if anybody else could
upload the fix, please.

Thanks a lot

Sincerely

Karl-Heinz
